summary: Algeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says that, except for those not subject to this formality, foreigners wishing to travel to Algeria must first obtain a visa from diplomatic and consular posts. Algeria's embassy in Brussels says groups of tourists on trips organised through approved travel agencies to the great South can be issued a visa on arrival.

currencyLimits.text: The UK FCDO says to declare cash at your point of entry and exit if you carry more than 5,000 euros or the equivalent in other currencies, and that failing to declare, or declaring falsely, is an offence that may lead to criminal prosecution. It says only travellers with residency status may bring in and take out Algerian banknotes, up to a maximum of 10,000 dinars.

notes: Canada's travel advice says you must declare all foreign currency on arrival and report each exchange of currency made during your stay, and that on departure you must present the currency declaration form issued on arrival and bank receipts for all your exchange transactions. It says Algerian dinars cannot be taken out of the country.
The UK FCDO says there are strict rules about goods you can take into and out of Algeria, and that you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
Canada's travel advice says to always keep your medication in the original container and to carry a copy of your prescriptions.

overstay.text: A foreigner must leave Algeria when the visa or the legal permitted stay expires; the maximum stay per entry is 90 days. Unless the situation is regularised, a foreigner staying irregularly may be escorted to the border by order of the wali. The UK government says that an overstayer is likely to be detained by immigration police at the airport on departure and may face criminal prosecution and up to 3 months in prison.

safety.text: The UK advises against all travel within 30 km of Algeria's borders with Libya, Mauritania, Mali and Niger and parts of the Tunisian border, and against all but essential travel near the rest of the border with Tunisia.

idp.text: Algeria is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). Algeria's Highway Code (Law 26-09 of 12 May 2026, Official Journal No. 36) says a valid driving licence lawfully issued abroad is considered equivalent to the Algerian licence, subject to the principle of reciprocity, and that the recognition period is six months for non-resident citizens and non-resident foreigners; people residing abroad may drive in Algeria for up to one year if they hold a valid foreign licence and an international driving permit conforming to international standards.

tips.text: Algeria's embassy in Brussels says groups of tourists travelling within an organised framework, on trips organised through approved travel agencies to the great South, can be issued a visa on arrival with a validity not exceeding 30 days. The measure applies exclusively to the wilayas of Tamanrasset, Illizi, Tindouf, Adrar, Bechar, Timimoune, Djanet, Bordj Badji Mokhtar, Béni Abbès, Ain Salah and Touggourt.

Algeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says a tourist visa application must be accompanied either by a certificate of accommodation legalized by the town hall of the place of accommodation, or by a hotel reservation or a certificate from a travel agency specifying the nature and place of the trip.

Canada's travel advice says credit cards are usually accepted at major hotels but rarely in restaurants and other businesses, that currency exchange or purchase on the black market is illegal, that on departure you must present bank receipts for all your exchange transactions, and that Algerian dinars cannot be taken out of the country.

Australia's Smartraveller says do not travel to the area within 450 km of the borders with Mali and Niger, due to the high threat of terrorism and kidnapping, or within 100 km of the borders with Mauritania, Libya and Tunisia, due to the very high threat of terrorism and kidnapping.

Canada's travel advice says photographing sensitive installations, including military sites, government buildings and bridges, is prohibited, and Australia's Smartraveller says photographing sensitive sites, government and military buildings or security personnel is illegal.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Algeria?
faq.answer: Yes, unless your nationality is exempt. Algeria's embassy in Helsinki says that by default all non-Algerians need to apply for a visa, and that nationals of Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic, Tunisia, Malaysia, the Maldives, Mali and Seychelles do not. For Morocco, the Algerian state news agency APS reported on 26 September 2024 that the government decided to reinstate, with immediate effect, the entry visa requirement for all foreign nationals holding a Moroccan passport. Algeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says that, except for those not subject to this formality, foreigners must first obtain a visa from diplomatic and consular posts.

faq.question: Does Algeria have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Algeria's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says foreigners must first obtain a visa from diplomatic and consular posts, and that a regularization visa could be issued on arrival, exceptionally and in case of emergency, by the authorized authorities. No official source we could read describes an eVisa. Algeria's embassy in Brussels says groups of tourists on trips organised through approved travel agencies to the great South can be issued a visa on arrival.

faq.question: Can I get an Algerian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Only for trips to the great South: Algeria's embassy in Brussels says groups of tourists travelling within an organised framework, on trips organised through approved travel agencies, can be issued a visa on arrival with a validity not exceeding 30 days. The measure applies exclusively to destinations in the wilayas of Tamanrasset, Illizi, Tindouf, Adrar, Bechar, Timimoune, Djanet, Bordj Badji Mokhtar, Béni Abbès, Ain Salah and Touggourt; tours to other wilayas remain subject to the consular visa system.

faq.question: Can I use my credit card in Algeria?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says Algeria is a cash-based economy: credit cards are usually accepted at major hotels but rarely in restaurants and other businesses, and ATMs accepting foreign cards are available in banks and a few major hotels but are unreliable. It says that on departure you must present the currency declaration form issued on arrival and bank receipts for all your exchange transactions, and that Algerian dinars cannot be taken out of the country.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Algeria?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states Algeria's entry rule for Israeli passport holders.

countryFacts.driving.text: Art. 75. — Tout permis de conduire légalement délivré à un conducteur par un pays étranger, en cours de validité, et attestant son aptitude à conduire un véhicule à moteur, est considéré équivalent au permis de conduire algérien, sous réserve du principe de réciprocité.
